explicitLimitations: 119-pair sweeps prove default authentication guard behavior, not successful or resource-specific authorization for every route; dedicated positive controls cover named account/profile/channel/media/push operations. Unsupported methods and unknown endpoints are not counted as secure behavior.

Actual Miniflare R2 objects are put/read/listed/deleted and a missing-object fault returns404 while unrelated data/metadata survive. This does not prove deployed bucket privacy/IAM, remote R2 availability, atomic cross-service crash recovery or remote bucket consistency.

SQLite-backed media and push ownership survive full workerd recreation. The R2 harness does not expose persistent R2 configuration for recreation; R2 bucket restart durability and write/delete exception injection remain unverified.

No automatic media expiry, signed links or private upload metadata enumeration API is implemented. Removed canonical URLs and query variants are exercised; absent legacy list/download endpoints are not counted as security passes.

WebPush encryption/delivery/VAPID signing, expired provider response handling, retry policy and delivery preference enforcement are absent. Registration, disable, ownership and storage results do not establish notification delivery.
Secret exclusion is tested through actual REST/IRC responses; complete runtime log capture/signing credential leakage is not established.

Broad JOIN/PART/channel-creation flood policy, slow-consumer output pressure, repeated failing-RPC retry bounds, full log-growth stress, deployed DNS/SSRF behavior, and all session/hibernation variants are not established here. Existing local SSRF unit tests are not deployed DNS evidence.
Cookie authentication is absent (documented bearer-only policy); cross-origin/cookie rejection is tested, but a nonexistent cookie mutation/CSRF implementation is not marked passing.

Generated media/message/role/account IDs are asserted directly at runtime but not exported as request traces; routeBehavior contains only concrete deterministic request paths, not fabricated paths for runtime UUIDs.

The original bundle03 test failures are preserved; the first bundle04 diagnostic run also exposed fixture synchronization, JSON key order and required duplex issues that were corrected without changing security expectations or production permissions.
